UNITED STATES
DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR
FISH AND WILDLIFE SERVICE
Ecological Services
9A33 Fritz Lanham Building
819 Taylor Street
Fort Worth, Texas 76102
March 25, 1976
Col. Joe H. Sheard, District Engineer Corps of Engineers, U. S. Army P. O. Box 17300 Fort Worth, Tx. 76102
Dear Col. Sheard:
By letter dated March 16, 1976, Mr. Gordon A. Walhood officially advised the Service of Fort Worth District involvement in the preparation of an environmental impact statement for the addition of two hydroelectric generators to the Amistad Lake Project on the Rio Grande at Del Rio, Texas. The letter further solicited information pertaining to any land use plans of our organization in the affected areas or any environmental impacts about which we might have concerns.
In regard to land use plans of our organization which might be affected, we foresee no conflict. In regard to areas of environmental impact about which we might have concerns, there is one primary area of probable impact which should be closely scrutinized. Hydroelectric operation will alter the pattern of downstream flows and may alter the fluctuation pattern of Amistad Reservoir itself. Flow patterns downstream as well as the alteration of reservoir fluctuation patterns could have a profound effect on existing fishery resources.
In an effort to provide meaningful input into the planning process for the project in question, we believe that considerable effort on our part, including participation in the flow release studies scheduled for April and May, would be required. For us to provide meaningful input to the stream flow-reservoir fluctuation question as it relates to fishery resources would require the availability of funding to defer costs. In this regard we estimate the need for a field level transfer of $3,500 from your District to our Fort Worth Office.
The expenditures of funds would occur during the period April through June, 1976.
John G. Degani
Sincerely,
Field Supervisor
WENCENTENN 1776-1976
